provenance: [REVIEWED] The fix named by RESIDUAL_PURITY_VERDICT.md as follow-up 1 — 'List-ALL-things elicitation (v2 proposal). The flame and the cello are one failure with one fix. This is now the highest-value change to the noun instrument.' Round `residual-purity-1` put 25 three-panel residual sheets in front of the reviewer and four classes of thing survived subtraction; two of them — a flame and a cello — survived for one structural reason, stated in that document: 'The noun question asks for *the* main thing in the cover. A second depicted object is never named, so it is never prompted, so it is never masked.' This set asks the same open-vocabulary question as `subject-noun.v1` and lifts exactly that limit: every distinct thing, not one. It does NOT supersede `subject-noun.v1` — that set's single noun stays the record of what a single-noun elicitation produces, and the v4-vs-v5 SAM comparison is only readable because both exist.
design_notes: ONE QUESTION, ONE VARIANT, and the same cost decision with the same name as `subject-noun.v1`. Per-inference cost on this model is dominated by image encode and prefill; decode length is small beside it. [MEASURED subject-noun-1, 2026-08-03] the single-noun pass ran 142 covers in 318.4 s, 2.24 s/inference, at ~9 generated tokens. This set's answer is a list, so decode grows — bounded by max_tokens 128 below — and the pass is budgeted at the same order. The marginal cost of a VARIANT is a whole extra pass, and the authorised budget for this run buys one. Hence variant J alone.

NO INTER-VARIANT AGREEMENT SIGNAL, stated as loudly here as in `subject-noun.v1`. ORACLE_QUESTION_SET.md design rule 7 gets uncertainty from disagreement between two phrasings. This set ships ONE variant and therefore has none: a list from this run is a single reading, not a corroborated one. The SAM-side derivation records that provenance separately so no analysis can pool a J list with an E==F agreed class word as if they carried the same weight. A second variant over the same covers is the cheapest available upgrade and is a follow-up, not something smuggled in under this budget.

VARIANT LETTER J, deliberately skipping H and I. `subject-noun.v1`'s own design notes reserve H: 'A second variant (H) over the same covers is the cheapest available upgrade and is left as a follow-up.' Taking H here would silently consume a reserved identity for a DIFFERENT schema. I is skipped because it is visually ambiguous with the digit 1 in run logs and row keys, which carry variant letters verbatim.

A JSON ARRAY ENVELOPE, and the grammar constrains ONLY the envelope. `subject-noun.v1` §FREE TEXT records why the answer space must be the model's whole vocabulary — the closed enum's most common answer, `object`, masked nothing at all (0 of 24 covers, 22 returning no region even at the 0.3 capture floor), because it is a grammatical category and not a thing-word. Nothing about that changes when the answer becomes a list. So: one object, one key, an array of strings, minItems 1, maxItems 8 — and never a constraint on a noun. `uniqueItems` is NOT declared: llguidance 1.7.6 does not implement it (`common.py` records that declaring it makes the grammar fail to build at the first token of the run), so distinctness is a PROMPT rule enforced at derivation time, not a grammar rule.

max_tokens 128, against `subject-noun.v1`'s 32 and the module default of 256. Eight two-word entries inside a single-key JSON array is ~55 tokens at the pinned tokenizer, so 128 is a little over 2x headroom on the worst case the grammar permits and still bounds a runaway decode to a few seconds. It is a cap, not a cost: greedy decoding stops at the grammar's closing bracket long before it.

THE THREE RULES OF `subject-noun.v1` ARE CARRIED OVER VERBATIM IN SUBSTANCE, because each is a measured failure and none of them stops applying to a list. (1) WHOLE, NOT PART — PROBE5's one finding against the design: `eye` scores 0.87-0.92 on eyes that are 0.1% of a frame and 0.42 on a cover that IS an eye, because a part noun makes a part detector. A list makes this rule MORE load-bearing, not less: the obvious failure mode of 'name everything' is a model that decomposes one subject into its parts, so the rule gains a second sentence forbidding exactly that. (2) SPECIFIC AS A CAPTION — the species noun is the half that carries the weight: 25 of 27 targets above the calibrated cut at a median 0.858, and where both fire the species beats the class word (castle 0.87 vs building 0.78; church 0.91 vs building 0.86). (3) The plural clause of `subject-noun.v1` is REPLACED, not dropped — see the next note.

THE PLURAL RULE CHANGES, AND THAT IS THE ONE PLACE THIS SET DEPARTS FROM ITS PARENT. `subject-noun.v1` carries ORACLE_QUESTION_SET.md §A.6.0's referent rule byte-identically: 'When there is more than one, take them all together — except where a single kind of thing is asked for, and then name the kind of the largest one.' That clause exists because ONE slot had to hold an answer for a cover with a person AND a car. This set has eight slots, so the presupposition it was defending against cannot arise, and carrying the clause over would actively suppress the second object this whole set exists to elicit. What replaces it is a DISTINCTNESS rule — one entry per kind, three birds is one entry — which keeps the referent well-defined per entry without collapsing distinct kinds together. The deviation is recorded below because the referent rule was earned the hard way and must not be seen to have been dropped by accident.

LARGEST FIRST, and the order is DATA, not presentation. PROBE5's salience findings and the residual experiment both turn on which thing dominates a cover; the SAM side stores each noun's rank in its own tag (`dyn-noun-1` .. `dyn-noun-8`), so a downstream consumer can ask 'the primary subject' of a list answer without re-deriving it. An unordered list would throw that away for nothing — the model is looking at the cover and is the only party in the pipeline that can order it cheaply.

A CAP OF EIGHT, and it is a recall/precision choice with a stated direction. The residual experiment is SUBTRACTION-oriented: an unnamed object is an object that survives into the residual, which is the failure `residual-purity-1` measured, so the cap errs high rather than low. It is not unbounded because the tail of an eight-item list on an album cover is small background detail whose masks would be noise, and because every entry is a SAM prompt whose GPU cost is real. Eight is the number the PROBE5 rules propose; nothing measured it, and it is flagged as an untested constant rather than dressed up as one.

AN ESCAPE HATCH IS STILL REQUIRED, for the reason `subject-noun.v1` gives: a closed enum can offer `not_applicable`; an open string cannot, and a model asked to name things on a cover that has none will invent them — which in this pipeline means a fabricated SAM prompt and a mask that should not exist. Under an array envelope with minItems 1 the empty list is not sayable, so the escape is a one-element list holding the literal `none`, and the derivation treats it as no-noun rather than as a noun. This is the same word, the same literal and the same treatment as the parent set, so the two runs' escapes are directly comparable.

NOTHING IS ASKED THAT ANOTHER SET ALREADY ANSWERS. No `has_dominant_subject` gate, no `subject_kind`, no area band. All three exist for these covers under `group-bcde.v1` with an E/F agreement rate already measured. Re-asking them here would spend the same GPU to produce a second, weaker reading of a question that has one.

NO `confidence` FIELD, same reason as `group-bcde.v1` and `subject-noun.v1`: measured degenerate under group-a.v1 (298 of 299 rows said `high`). Uncertainty about a noun shows up as SAM silence, which PROBE5 established is a real and separate signal — 'a null means no answer, not the VLM was wrong'.
deviations: THE §A.6.0 REFERENT CLAUSE IS REPLACED BY A DISTINCTNESS RULE. `subject-noun.v1` and both `group-bcde.v1` variants share the THE MAIN SUBJECT block byte-identically, including 'When there is more than one, take them all together — except where a single kind of thing is asked for, and then name the kind of the largest one.' This set does not carry that sentence. Reason in full in the design note above: the clause defends a one-slot answer against a multi-subject cover, this set has eight slots, and keeping it would suppress the very second object the set exists to elicit. CONSEQUENCE FOR JOINING: a J list and an E/F class word are no longer gathered under an identical referent rule, so the two must not be joined per cover as if they were. The SAM-side derivation keeps them in separate tags with separate provenance and never merges them into one answer.

FREE-TEXT ARRAY CANONICAL FIELD. `subject_nouns_all` is the first canonical field whose value is a LIST OF FREE TEXT. `common.validate_and_canonicalize` handles two shapes today: a single free-text string, and a `multi_select_fields` array whose items are checked against a closed vocabulary. Neither fits — this is an array whose items must NOT be checked against any vocabulary. The runner `run_premise_allnouns.py` supplies the third shape rather than editing `common.py`, and derives which fields take it from the variant's OWN json_schema (canonical field in `free_text_fields` AND schema type `array`), so the prompt document remains the single source of truth for its own answer shape.

`face` IS ABSENT FROM THE THING ENUMERATION, exactly as in `subject-noun.v1`. The shared THE MAIN SUBJECT block lists 'a face' as a subject, which is precisely what the WHOLE-NOT-PART rule forbids and what PROBE5 measured as a part detector. It is dropped here for the same reason and the deviation is recorded so the omission reads as deliberate.
system: You label album cover artwork for a research dataset. You answer with a list of nouns and nothing else. You never explain, never add fields, never write a sentence.
prompt:
Look at this album cover.

One question: list every distinct thing pictured.

WHAT COUNTS AS A THING. Something the cover depicts: a person, an animal, an object, a vehicle, a building, a plant, a natural feature. Lettering is not a thing. A pattern is not a thing. A colour, a texture or a plain field is not a thing.

EVERY DISTINCT THING, NOT ONLY THE MAIN ONE. This is the whole question. On a cover showing a man holding a cello beside a burning candle, all three are entries: man, cello, candle. Do not stop after the biggest thing.

THE WHOLE THING, NOT A PART OF IT. Name each thing itself, never a piece of it. On a cover showing a woman the entry is woman, not eye, not hand, not face, not hair. On a cover showing a bird the entry is bird, not wing, not beak, not feather. A part of something is never an entry. Once you have named a thing, do not add its parts as further entries.

ONE ENTRY PER KIND. Where several of the same kind are pictured, name that kind once: three birds is one entry, bird. Never name the same thing twice in different words.

LARGEST FIRST. Put the thing that takes up most of the cover first, and order the rest after it by how much of the cover they take up.

AT MOST EIGHT. Give the eight largest and stop. A small background detail is not worth an entry.

ONE OR TWO WORDS EACH. No sentence. No article. No number. Do not describe the colour, the style, the mood or the setting. Use a second word only where it is needed to say what the thing is, as in electric guitar or cassette tape.

AS SPECIFIC AS A CAPTION. Say what each thing actually is, in the ordinary words someone would use writing a caption for it: dalmatian rather than animal, cognac bottle rather than object, church rather than building, sports car rather than vehicle. Do not use a bare category word — animal, object, vehicle, building, structure, thing, subject, item, shape, figure — when a plainer and more specific name exists.

NOTHING PICTURED. If there is no thing on this cover at all — only lettering, only a pattern, only a plain or textured field, only a form you could not put a name to — give a list holding exactly this one word: none

1. all_things — every distinct thing pictured, largest first.

Reply with JSON only.
